title: Βάτραχοι ⟨ἐν λίμνῃ⟩
part: The Frogs and the Well (Chambry 68 · Perry 43)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 68 (= Perry 43). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« », ⟨ ⟩ for editorial supplements). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.l: Two frogs lived in a pond.
sentences.n: Chambry's Greek title reads Βάτραχοι ⟨ἐν λίμνῃ⟩; the angle brackets mark words he supplies himself to tell the several frog fables apart.

sentences.t: Θέρους δὲ ξηρανθείσης τῆς λίμνης, ἐκείνην καταλιπόντες ἐπεζήτουν ἑτέραν.
sentences.tr: Therous de xērantheisēs tēs limnēs, ekeinēn katalipontes epezētoun heteran.
sentences.l: And, the pond having dried up in the summer, leaving that one they went looking for another.
sentences.i: But in summer the pond dried up, and they left it and went in search of another.
sentences.n: Θέρους is a genitive of time within which, 'in the course of the summer'. ξηρανθείσης τῆς λίμνης is a genitive absolute — the standard way of setting the circumstance before the main clause.

sentences.t: Καὶ δὴ βαθεῖ περιέτυχον φρέατι, ὅπερ ἰδὼν ἅτερος θατέρῳ φησί· « Συγκατέλθωμεν, ὦ οὗτος, εἰς τόδε τὸ φρέαρ. »
sentences.tr: Kai dē bathei perietychon phreati, hoper idōn hateros thaterōi phēsi· « Synkatelthōmen, ō houtos, eis tode to phrear. »
sentences.l: And so they came upon a deep well, and the one of them, seeing it, says to the other: « Let us go down together, you there, into this well. »
sentences.i: And they came upon a deep well, and one of them saw it and said to the other: « Let us go down into this well together, you there. »
sentences.n: περιτυγχάνω takes the dative, 'to fall in with'. φησί is a present dropped into past narrative at the moment of speech — Greek does this constantly and English cannot follow it. ἅτερος … θατέρῳ are ὁ ἕτερος and τῷ ἑτέρῳ run together by crasis. Συγκατέλθωμεν is a hortatory subjunctive, 'let us go down'.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ ὑπολαβὼν εἶπεν· « Ἂν οὖν καὶ τὸ ἐνθάδε ὕδωρ ξηρανθῇ, πῶς ἀναβησόμεθα ; »
sentences.tr: Ho de hypolabōn eipen· « An oun kai to enthade hydōr xēranthēi, pōs anabēsometha ; »
sentences.l: And the other, taking him up, said: « If then the water here too should dry up, how shall we get back out? »
sentences.n: ὑπολαβών, 'having taken up the word', is the regular Greek way of introducing a reply that answers back. ἄν here is ἐάν; with the subjunctive and a future in the main clause it is the plain open condition about the future.

sentences.t: Ὁ μῦθος δηλοῖ ὅτι οὐ δεῖ ἀπερισκέπτως προσιέναι τοῖς πράγμασιν.
sentences.tr: Ho mythos dēloi hoti ou dei aperiskeptōs prosienai tois pragmasin.
sentences.l: The fable shows that one must not approach affairs without looking about one.
sentences.n: ἀπερίσκεπτος is literally 'not looking round about oneself' — the same figure the well supplies: they can see the water, not the way back up.
